To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

misonidozide (MIS) induces cell-cycle inhibition in human cells grown in vitro under aerobic condition and that this effect is phase-specific, since cells in mitosis and/or the early G1 phase are most susceptible to the effect.

misonidozide (MIS), a hypoxic cell sensitizer, in clinically relevant concentrations, induces cell cycle inhibition of human cells (NHLK 3025), when the cells are exposed to MIS under aerobic conditions.

misonidozide in clinically relevant concentrations (10(-5) to 10(-4)M) induces cell-kinetics changes in human cells, which seem to be a general prolongation of the cell-cycle, affecting all phases, but with a phase-dependent induction, only cells exposed to misonidazole during mitosis and early G1 will show significant cell-cycle prolongations.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of misonidazole on the cell cycle of human cells in vitro.
the effects of misonidazole, an agent with radiosensitizing properties, on the kinetics of the cell cycle.
the effect of the nitroimidazole radiosensitizer misonidazole on the cell cycle of cultured human cells under aerobic conditions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the effect of MIS in vivo may be a general cell cycle lengthening, but only cells exposed to the drug during the M/G1 phase will be affected.
MIS in clinically relevant concentrations has a significant cell-kinetic effect on human cells in vitro under aerobic culture conditions.
MIS is able to induce a cell cycle inhibition, which is dependent on phase of the cell cycle at the time of exposure, in exponentially growing human cells cultivated in aerobic conditions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
MIS in the concentration range 0-5 mM has a cell-cycle inhibitory effect on human cells grown in vitro under aerobic condition.
the cell-cycle effect of MIS seems to be a dose-dependent, reversible, phase-specific inhibition of cell proliferation.
the cytostatic effect of MIS on cells cultivated under aerobic conditions is due to a cell-kinetic effect, and that the effect is most pronounced in G0/G1.
The main takeaway from our work is that
misonidole can be used to study the cell cycle in human cells.
misonidazoles can have a significant effect on the cell cycle of human cells under aerobic conditions.
the cell cycle is a dynamic system that can be affected by many factors, including drugs like misonidazole.
